data.text: JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release. The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal. “The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision. “In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added. Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.” Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest. He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025. | via Janvic Mateo

output.verification_text:
JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.
The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.
“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.

claims.evidence_context:
JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.
The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.
“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.

“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.

output.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained — ICC trial chamber
output.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would war- rant his release. The decision on Duterte’s second review detention was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal. “The chamber finds that the prospect of the accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence , has increased. There is therefore, a likelihood of the accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” the five-page decision stated. “In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the prosecution’s submission of the witness and evidence lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases his ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added. Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of the detention.” Duterte, 81, appeared subdued as he sat in the last row of the defense section during the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case filed against him before the tribunal. Sporting a different hairstyle and dressed in a black suit and white shirt, the former president mainly listened as the parties discussed details of his upcoming trial, currently scheduled to begin on Nov. 30. ICC Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner did not directly address Duterte, but his presence was noted at the start of proceedings. In light of the developments following the annual hearing, the Chamber considers it necessary to give the parties and participants the opportunity to submit any observations they may have regarding the Accused’s continued detention or release, with or without conditions, including the existence of any changed circumstances.

text.preview: Ellen Tordesillas is president of VERA Files. A veteran reporter, she is the 1998 Marshall McLuhan fellow. Ellen Tordesillas is president of VERA Files. A veteran reporter, she is the 1998 Marshall McLuhan fellow. The newly-formed Trial Chamber III of the International Criminal Court ordered on May 1 parties concerned in the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte to submit observations on his situation at the Scheveningen prison in The Hague, Netherlands as required by the Court’s rules and regulations. “The Chamber observes that, pursuant to the statutory framework, the Accused’s pre-trial detention shall be reviewed at least every 120 days. In light of the developments following the annual hearing, the Chamber considers it necessary to give the parties and participants the opportunity to submit any observations they may have regarding the Accused’s continued detention or release, with or without conditions, including the existence of any changed circumstances,” the order, signed by Presiding Judge Joanna Korner and the two other members of the chamber, Keebong Paek and Nicolas Guillou, stated. Duterte, facing charges of crimes against humanity in connection with his war on drugs campaign between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019 has been in detention since March 12, 2025. He was arrested in the Philippines on March 11, 2025 on the strength of a March 7, 2025 warrant issued by the ICC and surrendered to the Court upon arrival in The Hague. Duterte’s only appearance while in detention took place on 14 March 2025 via video link. He has waived his right to appear in subsequent court proceedings. Despite claims by Duterte’s counsel Nicholas Kaufman that his 81-year old client is “enfeebled”, the Pre-Trial Chamber I reviewed his health and detention situation and found him fit to stand the confirmation proceedings that took place on Feb. 23 to 27. In an eight-page decision dated May 22, the ICC Trial Chamber III said there was no notable change in circumstance that would justify Duterte’s release, either with or without conditions. articles.description: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would war- rant his release.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would war- rant his release. The decision on Duterte’s second review detention was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal. “The chamber finds that the prospect of the accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence , has increased. There is therefore, a likelihood of the accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” the five-page decision stated. “In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the prosecution’s submission of the witness and evidence lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases his ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added. Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of the detention.” Duterte, 81, appeared subdued as he sat in the last row of the defense section during the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case filed against him before the tribunal. Sporting a different hairstyle and dressed in a black suit and white shirt, the former president mainly listened as the parties discussed details of his upcoming trial, currently scheduled to begin on Nov. 30. ICC Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner did not directly address Duterte, but his presence was noted at the start of proceedings. articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained — ICC trial chamber
articles.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

articles.description: Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

text.preview:
Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

In its decision, the ICC Trial Chamber III said the defense's and the ICC Registry's observations on Duterte's health condition "do not present information that constitute new facts or a change in circumstances in comparison to the information" submitted by the Court-appointed medical experts.

It also cited Duterte's refusal to recognize the jurisdiction of the ICC over him.

"Such statement demonstrates at its lowest that the accused will not comply with any orders that might be made in respect of a release from custody," the Court said.

"Taken together with his access to vast resources and contacts, including his family and supporters in the Philippines who may assist him in evading justice, the Chamber finds that, notwithstanding the defense's submissions regarding the accused’s health condition, there is a real and substantial risk that the accused could nonetheless abscond or obstruct justice either on his own or through his associates," it added.

"Consequently, the Chamber finds that the accused’s physical condition and cognitive capacities referred to by the defense do not constitute factors which outweigh the risks outlined above."

Earlier, the ICC Registry said that the 81-year-old Duterte is under cell monitoring due to his status as an elderly detained person with increased fall risk because of age and several chronic physical ailments.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

article.title: ICC chamber orders continued detention of Rodrigo Duterte
article.description: Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

text.preview:
Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

In its decision, the ICC Trial Chamber III said the defense's and the ICC Registry's observations on Duterte's health condition "do not present information that constitute new facts or a change in circumstances in comparison to the information" submitted by the Court-appointed medical experts.

It also cited Duterte's refusal to recognize the jurisdiction of the ICC over him.

"Such statement demonstrates at its lowest that the accused will not comply with any orders that might be made in respect of a release from custody," the Court said.

"Taken together with his access to vast resources and contacts, including his family and supporters in the Philippines who may assist him in evading justice, the Chamber finds that, notwithstanding the defense's submissions regarding the accused’s health condition, there is a real and substantial risk that the accused could nonetheless abscond or obstruct justice either on his own or through his associates," it added.

"Consequently, the Chamber finds that the accused’s physical condition and cognitive capacities referred to by the defense do not constitute factors which outweigh the risks outlined above."

Earlier, the ICC Registry said that the 81-year-old Duterte is under cell monitoring due to his status as an elderly detained person with increased fall risk because of age and several chronic physical ailments.

article.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained — ICC trial chamber
article.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

claim.normalized_claim: Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after ICC trial judges found no notable change in circumstances that would warrant his release.

source_passages.quote: JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.

claim.evidence_context:
JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.
The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.
“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.

The ICC's Trial Chamber III had released its second decision on the review of Duterte's detention after the third status conference on his case, where the former Philippine leader made an in-person appearance. In reviewing the developments after its first decision on the review of Duterte's detention , the Chamber noted that there is "a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings." With the prosecution having submitted its Witness and Evidence Lists, the Chamber also noted that this "increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines." Duterte's defense team said on Tuesday that the former president is suffering from severe memory loss, sometimes forgetting his lawyer's name. article.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained — ICC trial chamber
article.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

article.title: ICC chamber orders continued detention of Rodrigo Duterte
article.description: Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

text.preview:
Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

In its decision, the ICC Trial Chamber III said the defense's and the ICC Registry's observations on Duterte's health condition "do not present information that constitute new facts or a change in circumstances in comparison to the information" submitted by the Court-appointed medical experts.

It also cited Duterte's refusal to recognize the jurisdiction of the ICC over him.

"Such statement demonstrates at its lowest that the accused will not comply with any orders that might be made in respect of a release from custody," the Court said.

"Taken together with his access to vast resources and contacts, including his family and supporters in the Philippines who may assist him in evading justice, the Chamber finds that, notwithstanding the defense's submissions regarding the accused’s health condition, there is a real and substantial risk that the accused could nonetheless abscond or obstruct justice either on his own or through his associates," it added.

"Consequently, the Chamber finds that the accused’s physical condition and cognitive capacities referred to by the defense do not constitute factors which outweigh the risks outlined above."

Earlier, the ICC Registry said that the 81-year-old Duterte is under cell monitoring due to his status as an elderly detained person with increased fall risk because of age and several chronic physical ailments.

article.description: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague ahead of his trial for crimes against humanity before the International Criminal Court, judges ruled on Friday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague ahead of his trial for crimes against humanity before the International Criminal Court (ICC), judges ruled on Friday. In an eight-page decision dated May 22, the ICC Trial Chamber III said there was no notable change in circumstance that would justify Duterte’s release, either with or without conditions. The judges stressed that the recent confirmation of charges against Duterte even “increases the risk that an accused may abscond and is therefore not a change in circumstances that militates in favor of conditional release, but rather one supporting continued detention.” They said Duterte’s refusal to attend his confirmation hearing in February and his statement that he does not recognize the jurisdiction of the ICC, “demonstrates at its lowest that the Accused will not comply with any orders that might be made in respect of a release from custody.” “Taken together with his access to vast resources and contacts, including his family and supporters in the Philippines who may assist him in evading justice, the chamber finds that… there is a real and substantial risk that the Accused could nonetheless abscond or obstruct justice either on his own or through his associates,” read the eight-page decision. text.preview: Ellen Tordesillas is president of VERA Files. A veteran reporter, she is the 1998 Marshall McLuhan fellow. Ellen Tordesillas is president of VERA Files. A veteran reporter, she is the 1998 Marshall McLuhan fellow. The newly-formed Trial Chamber III of the International Criminal Court ordered on May 1 parties concerned in the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte to submit observations on his situation at the Scheveningen prison in The Hague, Netherlands as required by the Court’s rules and regulations. “The Chamber observes that, pursuant to the statutory framework, the Accused’s pre-trial detention shall be reviewed at least every 120 days. In light of the developments following the annual hearing, the Chamber considers it necessary to give the parties and participants the opportunity to submit any observations they may have regarding the Accused’s continued detention or release, with or without conditions, including the existence of any changed circumstances,” the order, signed by Presiding Judge Joanna Korner and the two other members of the chamber, Keebong Paek and Nicolas Guillou, stated. Duterte, facing charges of crimes against humanity in connection with his war on drugs campaign between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019 has been in detention since March 12, 2025. Despite claims by Duterte’s counsel Nicholas Kaufman that his 81-year old client is “enfeebled”, the Pre-Trial Chamber I reviewed his health and detention situation and found him fit to stand the confirmation proceedings that took place on Feb. 23 to 27. articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained — ICC trial chamber
articles.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

text.preview:
Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

In its decision, the ICC Trial Chamber III said the defense's and the ICC Registry's observations on Duterte's health condition "do not present information that constitute new facts or a change in circumstances in comparison to the information" submitted by the Court-appointed medical experts.

It also cited Duterte's refusal to recognize the jurisdiction of the ICC over him.

The application always includes the entire input through its final word. Never rewrite any text. Keep negation, speaker, recipient and qualifiers. The newly-formed Trial Chamber III of the International Criminal Court ordered on May 1 parties concerned in the trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte to submit observations on his situation at the Scheveningen prison in The Hague, Netherlands as required by the Court’s rules and regulations.

“The Chamber observes that, pursuant to the statutory framework, the Accused’s pre-trial detention shall be reviewed at least every 120 days. In light of the developments following the annual hearing, the Chamber considers it necessary to give the parties and participants the opportunity to submit any observations they may have regarding the Accused’s continued detention or release, with or without conditions, including the existence of any changed circumstances,” the order, signed by Presiding Judge Joanna Korner and the two other members of the chamber, Keebong Paek and Nicolas Guillou, stated.
Duterte, facing charges of crimes against humanity in connection with his war on drugs campaign between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019 has been in detention since March 12, 2025.
He was arrested in the Philippines on March 11, 2025 on the strength of a March 7, 2025 warrant issued by the ICC and surrendered to the Court upon arrival in The Hague.
Duterte’s only appearance while in detention took place on 14 March 2025 via video link.
He has waived his right to appear in subsequent court proceedings.

Despite claims by Duterte’s counsel Nicholas Kaufman that his 81-year old client is “enfeebled”, the Pre-Trial Chamber I reviewed his health and detention situation and found him fit to stand the confirmation proceedings that took place on Feb. 23 to 27.
The findings were affirmed by the mandatory annual review which took place on Feb. 27.
Preparation for Duterte’s trial has started after the Pre-Trial Chamber I unanimously confirmed all the charges comprised of three counts of crimes against humanity.
Trial Chamber III has called for a First Status Conference among parties concerned on May 27 to decide, among other matters, the date of the trial;
estimated number of witnesses to be called and number of hours of in-court testimony;
use of expert witnesses;
testimony given by audio or video link;
estimated volume of documentary and other non-testimonial evidence to be relied upon at trial.

Situation in the Republic of the Philippines The Prosecutor v.

Rodrigo Roa Duterte ICC-01/21-01/25 Updated: February 2026 Suspected of the crimes against humanity of murder and attempted murder, allegedly committed in the Republic of the Philippines between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019.
Surrendered to the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on 12 March 2025.
Confirmation of charges hearing to open on 23 February 2026.

Date of birth: 28 March 1945 Nationality: national of the Republic of the Philippines Function(s) at the time of the alleged crimes: President of the Philippines, Mayor of Davao City, Vice Mayor of Davao City, and allegedly the founder and head of the Davao Death Squad (‘DDS’).

Arrest warrant: issued on 7 March 2025 Surrender to ICC Custody: 12 March 2025 Initial appearance: 14 March 2025 Confirmation of charges hearing: scheduled on 23-27 February 2026 According to the Prosecution’s submission of the Document Containing the Charges, Mr Duterte is suspected of 3 counts of crimes against humanity allegedly committed from at least 1 November 2011 to 16 March 2019 in the Philippines: Key judicial developments OPENING OF THE INVESTIGATION On 24 May 2021, the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICC (“the Prosecution”) requested authorisation from the Chamber to initiate an investigation into crimes allegedly committed on the territory of the Philippines in the context of the “war on drugs” campaign waged by the Government of the Philippines between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019.
On 14 June 2021, the Prosecution’s request was made public.
On 15 September 2021, Pre-Trial Chamber I authorised the investigation.

On 18 July 2023, following the Philippine authorities’ request for deferral and the subsequent temporary suspension of the investigative activities, the ICC Appeals Chamber delivered its judgment which confirmed the Chamber’s decision granting authorisation to the Prosecution to resume the investigation in relation to the situation in the Philippines.
The Philippines, an ICC State Party since 1 November 2011, deposited a written notification of withdrawal from the Statute on 17 March 2018.
Under article 127 of the Statute, that withdrawal took effect on 17 March 2019.
Nevertheless, the ICC retains jurisdiction over crimes allegedly committed in the Philippines while the country was a State Party to the Statute.
On 10 February 2025, the Prosecution applied for an arrest warrant against Mr Duterte for the crimes against humanity of murder, torture and rape.

Having assessed the material submitted by the Prosecution, Pre-Trial Chamber I found reasonable grounds to believe that Mr Duterte is individually responsible as an indirect co-perpetrator for the crime against humanity of murder, allegedly committed in the Philippines between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019.
The warrant of arrest against Mr Duterte was issued by the Chamber as “Secret” on 7 March 2025 and reclassified as “Public” on 11 March 2025.

On 12 March 2025, Mr Duterte was surrendered to the International Criminal Court, after being arrested by the authorities of the Republic of the Philippines in accordance with the warrant of arrest issued by Pre-Trial Chamber I. He is currently in ICC custody.

The initial appearance of Mr Duterte took place on 14 March 2025 before Pre-Trial Chamber I. Mr Duterte appeared in the hearing via video link from the ICC Detention Centre, as authorised by the Chamber.

The Chamber verified the identity of the suspect and ensured that he was clearly informed of the crimes he is alleged to have committed and of his rights under the Rome Statute of the ICC in a language he fully understands and speaks.
On 8 September 2025, Pre-Trial Chamber I postponed the commencement of the confirmation hearing in the case, which had been initially scheduled to start on 23 September 2025.

Following a request from the Defence of Mr Duterte for an indefinite adjournment of the proceedings alleging that Mr Duterte is not fit to stand trial, the majority of the Chamber considered that a limited postponement of the hearing on the confirmation of charges was warranted to allow sufficient time to adjudicate the request and related matters.
On 26 January 2026, Pre-Trial Chamber I found Mr Rodrigo Roa Duterte fit to take part in the pre-trial proceedings and rejected the Defence’s request for an indefinite adjournment.

Having regard to the relevant legal principles, the medical assessment of a panel of three independent medical experts and all of the relevant circumstances of the case, the Chamber was satisfied that Mr Duterte is able effectively to exercise his procedural rights and is therefore fit to take part in the pre-trial proceedings, which are thereby resumed.
The Chamber has scheduled the confirmation of charges hearing for 23 to 27 February 2026.

The purpose of the confirmation of charges procedure is to determine whether there is sufficient evidence to establish substantial grounds to believe that the person committed the crimes he or she is suspected of.
If the charges are confirmed, totally or partly, the case will be transferred to a Trial Chamber, which will conduct the subsequent phase of the proceedings: the trial.
The Chamber will issue its decision on the confirmation of charges within 60 days after the confirmation hearing.
The judges have allowed victims to participate in the proceedings.

In this case, the judges appointed Joel Butuyan and Gilbert Andres, as well as Paolina Massidda of the Office of the Public Counsel for Victims (OPCV) as a single team of common legal representatives for any admitted victims.

Familiarity with security threats does not by itself establish questioning about personal biography/background. Nearby dates do not prove a stated causal explanation. article.title: Rodrigo Duterte to remain detained — ICC trial chamber
article.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

article.title: ICC chamber orders continued detention of Rodrigo Duterte
article.description: Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

text.preview:
Former President Rodrigo Duterte will continue to be detained in The Hague pending the start of his trial for alleged crimes against humanity, the International Criminal Court (ICC) said Friday.

In its decision, the ICC Trial Chamber III said the defense's and the ICC Registry's observations on Duterte's health condition "do not present information that constitute new facts or a change in circumstances in comparison to the information" submitted by the Court-appointed medical experts.

It also cited Duterte's refusal to recognize the jurisdiction of the ICC over him.

"Such statement demonstrates at its lowest that the accused will not comply with any orders that might be made in respect of a release from custody," the Court said.

"Taken together with his access to vast resources and contacts, including his family and supporters in the Philippines who may assist him in evading justice, the Chamber finds that, notwithstanding the defense's submissions regarding the accused’s health condition, there is a real and substantial risk that the accused could nonetheless abscond or obstruct justice either on his own or through his associates," it added.

"Consequently, the Chamber finds that the accused’s physical condition and cognitive capacities referred to by the defense do not constitute factors which outweigh the risks outlined above."

Earlier, the ICC Registry said that the 81-year-old Duterte is under cell monitoring due to his status as an elderly detained person with increased fall risk because of age and several chronic physical ailments.

source_passages.quote: The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.

claim.evidence_context:
JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.
The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.
“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.

output.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

text.preview: A smiling Rodrigo Duterte sat through more than an hour of proceedings at the International Criminal Court on Wednesday, marking the former president’s first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025. Dressed in black suit and white polo shirt, Duterte appeared attentive as Trial Chamber III tackled procedural and administrative issues ahead of his Nov. 30 trial on crimes against humanity. Photographs released after the hearing showed Duterte walking without a wheelchair and without eyeglasses. He appeared thinner and sported a grayish stubble beard, with thick, dark brown hair noticeably different from his usual style before his arrest, prompting speculations that he may have been wearing a wig. The appearance was Duterte’s first before the ICC in person since March 14, 2025, when he joined his initial hearing before the Pre-Trial Chamber I by video link from detention. At that hearing, he looked drowsy and spoke slowly while confirming his identity before the judges, in contrast to his more attentive demeanor throughout the status conference. At the start of the hearing, Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joana Korner told Duterte that he could leave the courtroom at any time without asking permission, indicating the court’s willingness to consider his medical limitations while maintaining his participation. “This is the first time that Mr. Duterte has been in this court. As far as the trial chamber is concerned, if he wishes to leave for any reason, he may do so,” Korner said. But Duterte did not leave and sat through the end of the third status conference. On the same day, however, the trial chamber ordered Duterte’s continued detention while awaiting trial, citing the risk that he may abscond, obstruct, or endanger the investigations given the recent developments on his case. output.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has directed concerned parties to submit their observations on the continued detention of former president Rodrigo Duterte by May 8, following the confirmation of charges against him.

text.preview:
The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has directed concerned parties to submit their observations on the continued detention of former president Rodrigo Duterte by May 8, following the confirmation of charges against him.

In an order dated May 1, the Chamber identified the parties as the Office of the Prosecutor, Duterte’s defense counsel, the Legal Representatives of the Victims, and the Office of the Public Counsel for Victims.

“The Chamber observes that, pursuant to the statutory framework, the Accused’s pre-trial detention shall be reviewed at least every 120 days,” the ICC said.

“In light of the developments following the annual hearing, the Chamber considers it necessary to give the parties and participants the opportunity to submit any observations they may have regarding the Accused’s continued detention or release, with or without conditions, including the existence of any changed circumstances,” it added.

Trial Chamber III is set to hold a status conference on May 27 on the crimes against humanity charges linked to Duterte’s war on illegal drugs.

The proceedings will be streamed on the ICC website with a 30-minute delay.

On April 23, the ICC confirmed charges of crimes against humanity against the 81-year-old Duterte.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would war- rant his release. The decision on Duterte’s second review detention was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal. “The chamber finds that the prospect of the accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence , has increased. There is therefore, a likelihood of the accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” the five-page decision stated. “In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the prosecution’s submission of the witness and evidence lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases his ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added. Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of the detention.” Duterte, 81, appeared subdued as he sat in the last row of the defense section during the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case filed against him before the tribunal. Sporting a different hairstyle and dressed in a black suit and white shirt, the former president mainly listened as the parties discussed details of his upcoming trial, currently scheduled to begin on Nov. 30. ICC Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner did not directly address Duterte, but his presence was noted at the start of proceedings. output.title: ICC sets 3rd status conference on Duterte case
output.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will hold on Wednesday the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will hold on Wednesday the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte. The conference, scheduled to start 10:30 a.m. in The Hague (4:30 p.m. in Manila), will be livestreamed online with a 30-minute delay. It will tackle details of the prosecution’s case, including its list of witnesses and evidence, the number of hours to be given to the prosecutor, the ongoing disclosure to the defense and other possible incidents to be added in the case. The parties will also discuss the trial schedule, which will start on Nov. 30, including the proposal to have “blocks of hearings with breaks.” It remains unclear if Duterte will be present as he was previously allowed to skip the pre-trial proceedings. But during the last status conference on June 23, presiding judge Joanna Korner said they expect Duterte to attend the September status conference “unless there’s some medical issue” that would prevent him from doing so. Duterte has never appeared in person before ICC judges. He was last seen by the public on March 14, 2025, when he appeared via video link during his initial appearance hearing before the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I. text.preview: A man holds a portrait of former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte in front of the International Criminal Court (ICC) where he will be appearing, in The Hague on March 14, 2025. Nicolas Tucat, AFP/File MANILA -- The International Criminal Court (ICC) has allowed prosecutors to examine some materials taken from former president Rodrigo Roa Duterte following his arrest, while rejecting a separate request for access to all keys found among his belongings. The rulings, originally issued on May 28 and June 22 but released to the public in redacted form on Friday, showed that Trial Chamber III partly granted the prosecution's requests for materials kept by the ICC Registry in connection with its investigation into Duterte's alleged crimes against humanity. In its May 28 decision, the chamber granted the prosecution's request to inspect certain redacted materials recovered from Duterte's belongings after he was surrendered to the custody of the Court on March 12, 2025. The judges said there were reasonable grounds to believe the requested examination could produce evidence necessary for the investigation and found the request "necessary and proportionate" to the prosecution's investigative needs. The chamber also ordered prosecutors to submit, within one month after receiving the materials, a report detailing the measures taken to protect Duterte's private information. The judges, however, criticized the prosecution for waiting more than a year after being informed of the Registry's report before seeking access to the materials. "The Chamber deplores the fact that the Prosecution did not make this request at an earlier stage of the proceedings and provides no reason for this failure," the decision said. The chamber also granted prosecutors access to the Registry's inventory of items obtained from Duterte upon his arrest by ordering the reclassification of confidential Registry documents. text.preview: A smiling Rodrigo Duterte sat through more than an hour of proceedings at the International Criminal Court on Wednesday, marking the former president’s first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025. Dressed in black suit and white polo shirt, Duterte appeared attentive as Trial Chamber III tackled procedural and administrative issues ahead of his Nov. 30 trial on crimes against humanity. Photographs released after the hearing showed Duterte walking without a wheelchair and without eyeglasses. He appeared thinner and sported a grayish stubble beard, with thick, dark brown hair noticeably different from his usual style before his arrest, prompting speculations that he may have been wearing a wig. The appearance was Duterte’s first before the ICC in person since March 14, 2025, when he joined his initial hearing before the Pre-Trial Chamber I by video link from detention. At that hearing, he looked drowsy and spoke slowly while confirming his identity before the judges, in contrast to his more attentive demeanor throughout the status conference. At the start of the hearing, Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joana Korner told Duterte that he could leave the courtroom at any time without asking permission, indicating the court’s willingness to consider his medical limitations while maintaining his participation. “This is the first time that Mr. Duterte has been in this court. As far as the trial chamber is concerned, if he wishes to leave for any reason, he may do so,” Korner said. But Duterte did not leave and sat through the end of the third status conference. On the same day, however, the trial chamber ordered Duterte’s continued detention while awaiting trial, citing the risk that he may abscond, obstruct, or endanger the investigations given the recent developments on his case. text.preview:
The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has directed concerned parties to submit their observations on the continued detention of former president Rodrigo Duterte by May 8, following the confirmation of charges against him.

In an order dated May 1, the Chamber identified the parties as the Office of the Prosecutor, Duterte’s defense counsel, the Legal Representatives of the Victims, and the Office of the Public Counsel for Victims.

“The Chamber observes that, pursuant to the statutory framework, the Accused’s pre-trial detention shall be reviewed at least every 120 days,” the ICC said.

“In light of the developments following the annual hearing, the Chamber considers it necessary to give the parties and participants the opportunity to submit any observations they may have regarding the Accused’s continued detention or release, with or without conditions, including the existence of any changed circumstances,” it added.

Trial Chamber III is set to hold a status conference on May 27 on the crimes against humanity charges linked to Duterte’s war on illegal drugs.

The proceedings will be streamed on the ICC website with a 30-minute delay.

On April 23, the ICC confirmed charges of crimes against humanity against the 81-year-old Duterte.

articles.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

text.preview:
THE HAGUE – The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III has unanimously decided to keep former President Rodrigo Duterte detained.

In a decision released shortly after the conclusion of the third status conference, the Chamber found a likelihood of Duterte “absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings.”

“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution’s submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused’s ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” the decision read.

The Chamber noted it has yet to decide on the issue of Duterte’s fitness, as the defense’s requested “greater medical certainty” while challenging the expert panel’s report.

However, the Chamber said the observations of Duterte’s lawyers “do not provide any information that constitutes new facts or a change in circumstances” which would warrant a modification of his detention.

The ICC Office of the Prosecutor is asking the Trial Chamber III to order the continued detention of Duterte, noting that it is “necessary” so he would not “interfere with witnesses.”

Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang said “there has been no change” in Duterte’s circumstances that would prompt the Trial Chamber III to revise its previous order on the former president’s detention.

“To the contrary,” Niang noted in an observation filed on September 14, “there have been changes in circumstances that have increased the risk Mr. Duterte presents under articles 58(1)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Statute.”

articles.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will hold on Wednesday the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will hold on Wednesday the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte. The conference, scheduled to start 10:30 a.m. in The Hague (4:30 p.m. in Manila), will be livestreamed online with a 30-minute delay. It will tackle details of the prosecution’s case, including its list of witnesses and evidence, the number of hours to be given to the prosecutor, the ongoing disclosure to the defense and other possible incidents to be added in the case. The parties will also discuss the trial schedule, which will start on Nov. 30, including the proposal to have “blocks of hearings with breaks.” It remains unclear if Duterte will be present as he was previously allowed to skip the pre-trial proceedings. But during the last status conference on June 23, presiding judge Joanna Korner said they expect Duterte to attend the September status conference “unless there’s some medical issue” that would prevent him from doing so. Duterte has never appeared in person before ICC judges. He was last seen by the public on March 14, 2025, when he appeared via video link during his initial appearance hearing before the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I. value.text: JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release. The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal. “The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision. “In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added. Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.” Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest. He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025. | via Janvic Mateo

JUST IN: Former president Rodrigo Duterte will remain in detention in The Hague after trial judges of the International Criminal Court (ICC) found “no notable change” in circumstances that would warrant his release.
The decision on Duterte’s second detention review was released by the ICC Trial Chamber III hours after he appeared for the first time in person before the international tribunal.
“The Chamber finds that the prospect of the Accused facing a trial, and (in the event of a conviction), a lengthy prison sentence, has increased. There is, therefore, a likelihood of the Accused absconding and/or obstructing or endangering the investigation or the court proceedings,” read the five-page decision.
“In respect of the latter considerations, owing to the Prosecution's submission of the Witness and Evidence Lists, (thereby disclosing the identities of the witnesses and the contents of their expected testimony), this increases the Accused's ability to interfere with witnesses, either directly or through his family or supporters in the Philippines,” it added.
Although the decision on Duterte’s fitness to stand trial is still pending, the judges also ruled that the expert panel’s reports “do not contain any new information that warrants a modification of [Duterte’s] detention.”
Duterte has been detained at the ICC Detention Centre in The Hague since his arrest.
He was last seen by the public during his initial appearance hearing on March 14, 2025.
